heading_path: Scenario: Pre-computed IDs and the $transaction([]) API

content.text:
`updateMany` applies one `data` object to every matching row, so it can't give two groups different `order` values. To swap, use two `update` calls inside one `$transaction([])`, so both writes succeed or fail together:

```ts
await prisma.$transaction([
  prisma.todoGroup.update({ where: { id: a.id }, data: { order: b.order } }),
  prisma.todoGroup.update({ where: { id: b.id }, data: { order: a.order } }),
]);
```

The docs don't have a swap example. This is my adaptation of the independent-writes pattern in `apps/docs/content/docs/orm/v7/prisma-client/queries/transactions.mdx` (section "Independent writes → Pre-computed IDs and the $transaction([]) API"). The `updateMany` example in the "Marking emails as read" scenario there shows that it sets a single value on all matches. `order` isn't `@unique` in your schema, so the temporary duplicate value during the swap won't cause an error.
